title: Agents — the roster and what each is bound to

components.purpose: Show every agent on the account, what strategy each reads, and whether another can be created.
components.current_implementation: Bordered ul of li, styled with Tailwind (3.4.19, installed since this surface was first surveyed — the classes now render). Three top-level branches rendered separately — agents, empty, unreadable. The unreadable branch is role=alert and carries four lines: heading, the raw reason from the port, the why-not-loaded sentence, and a closing line stating what is unavailable. | agent-row: Bordered li; name and status on one baseline row, then the binding sentence. No truncation handling.
constraints: `empty` and `unreadable` are separate branches from the port and must stay visually distinct. Branching on `length === 0` makes an account whose roster failed to load look like an account with no agents, and telling that user they have none is how someone recreates work they already own — or concludes something deleted it

`unreadable` must keep stating what is unavailable as its own condition, not as a pronoun pointing at the sentence above it. It read 'nothing can be created or changed until it can' while the preceding clause was always 'could not reach BattleGrid'; once that clause started varying by cause, the antecedent disappeared. It is a capability statement, not only an error
`create-unknown` renders nothing at all. An affordance whose availability we do not know must not be guessed into existence
The capacity notice appears before the form, not after submission
[agent-row] The bound strategy *and its revision* must stay together — the revision is what tells a user whether this agent has picked up a recent edit
[agent-row] Status must not be signalled by colour alone
[agent-row] Long display names must not push the status out of view

components.purpose: Offer only the actions BattleGrid permits on this particular agent.
components.current_implementation: nav > ul of underlined anchors, labelled `Actions for <name>`. A trailing note when an active agent is not editable.
constraints: There is no delete action and there must never be one. The live payload sets `capabilities.canDelete: true` while the MCP surface offers no delete tool — the flag describes what BattleGrid's own app can do. A delete button would ship an action that cannot work (findings-agents F-1)
Journal is always offered, including on agents nothing else can be done to; it is the one affordance that never depends on permission
The 'BattleGrid does not permit Grid-Commander to change this agent' note must stay attached to the action list — it explains an absence, and an absence with no explanation reads as a missing feature
All actions are GET links to a page that asks first; none mutates on click

components.purpose: Tell a user their work still exists, and say accurately why it could not be shown.
components.current_implementation:
One

inside the unreadable branch of both the roster and the strategy list. The reassurance clause is fixed and outside the conditional; only the cause clause varies. Takes a `subject` string so the two callers share one sentence rather than holding two copies.
constraints: The reassurance ('this does not mean X are gone') must render in BOTH states. It is the only thing on screen telling a user their work still exists, and it sits outside the branch so neither case can be written without it

`refused` and `unreachable` must not be collapsed back into one sentence. A refusal means BattleGrid was reached and declined — waiting changes nothing and the credential is the fix. Unreachable means no usable answer came back — the credential may be fine and waiting may be exactly right. Naming the wrong one sends a user to wait for an outage that is not happening

Neither state may be softened into a vague 'something went wrong'. The sentence earns its reassurance by naming a cause that is obviously external and obviously not deletion; a vaguer cause is a weaker reassurance
The cause arrives as a value on the result. Nothing here may re-derive it by matching on the reason text

components.purpose: Turn away a request with no authority.
components.current_implementation: Shared component rendered in place of the page body. Reachable only on a delegated deployment: a personal one resolves the acting user from a configured key and never returns not-connected, so this page cannot render there.
constraints: One page for every cause; they differ in cause and not in remedy (design W-C)

accessibility.notes: Per-row nav labelled `Actions for <agent name>`. Roster failure is role=alert; capacity is role=status.
